resources.string: KakuKaku is running. Drag the box over Japanese text, then double-tap it.

KakuKaku looks up Japanese text from your screen. It is a continuation of Kaku by 0xbad1d3a5 (github.com/0xbad1d3a5/Kaku) and is not endorsed by its author. It works offline and collects no data.

Dictionary data
JMdict and KANJIDIC2 are the property of the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group (EDRDG) and are used under its licence (CC BY-SA 4.0), www.edrdg.org/edrdg/licence.html. The built-in dictionary is derived from them.

Conjugation rules
The deinflection rules (deinflect.dat) come from Rikaichan by Jonathan Zarate. Rikaichan is licensed under the GNU General Public License (version 2 or later); this file is not covered by the BSD licence below and keeps its original terms.

Libraries
Google ML Kit text recognition (Google terms), AndroidX and Material Components, Gson (Apache License 2.0), ORMLite (ISC licence).

KakuKaku does not include pitch accent data. Import a pitch accent dictionary in Yomitan format (a .zip with term_meta_bank_N.json files), for example one from the Yomitan wiki. The accent is shown after the reading, like 猫 (ねこ) [1].
JMdict is updated almost daily. Download JMdict_english.zip, then import it here to replace the old copy.

Import dictionaries in Yomitan format: a .zip file (not unpacked) with index.json and term_bank_N.json or kanji_bank_N.json files. Pitch accent dictionaries have their own import further down.

Find dictionaries on the Yomitan wiki, for example Jitendex, JMdict, JMnedict, KANJIDIC and Wiktionary.

Words are looked up in one dictionary at a time. Kanji details always come from the built-in dictionary.
Browse dictionaries on the Yomitan wiki
Delete \"%1$s\"? You can import it again later.
